definitions.explanation: A protective cover for a blade, especially a Japanese sword. Also used metaphorically in idiomatic expressions.
The outer casing of beans or peas. Used in cooking and agricultural contexts.

examples.japanese: {刀|かたな}を{鞘|さや}に{収|おさ}めた。
この{鞘|さや}は{漆|うるし}で{美|うつく}しく{塗|ぬ}られている。
{武士|ぶし}は{鞘|さや}から{刀|かたな}を{抜|ぬ}き、{静|しず}かに{構|かま}えた。
examples.english: The samurai drew his sword from the scabbard and quietly assumed a stance.

examples.japanese: えんどう{豆|まめ}の{鞘|さや}をむく。
{鞘|さや}つきのインゲンを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought green beans still in their pods.

examples.japanese: そら{豆|まめ}は{鞘|さや}から{出|だ}して{塩|しお}ゆでにすると{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: Broad beans are delicious when removed from the pod and boiled with salt.

notes:
Two distinct meanings connected by the concept of an outer covering.

SENSE 1 (sheath):
Central to Japanese sword culture. Appears in well-known idioms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sheath):
- {鞘|さや}に{収|おさ}める (sheathe; also figuratively: settle a dispute)
- {鞘|さや}から{抜|ぬ}く (draw from the scabbard)
- {鞘|さや}{当|あ}て (rivalry between two people, lit. scabbards bumping)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
{元|もと}の{鞘|さや}に{収|おさ}まる — to get back together (of a couple), literally "return to the original scabbard."

SENSE 2 (pod):
Used for beans, peas, and similar vegetables.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (pod):
- {鞘|さや}をむく (shell pods)
- {鞘|さや}つき (with pods still on)
- {鞘|さや}いんげん (string beans in pods)
